definitions.rationale: This is the negative-input branch of the piecewise fizzEnd summary, defining the final loop index as zero when the outer loop does not run.
This is the nonnegative-input branch of the piecewise fizzEnd summary, defining the final loop index as N.
This is the base equation for digitSevens, defining the decimal-seven count as zero once the nonnegative digit scan is exhausted.
This recurrence defines digitSevens for a positive integer whose last decimal digit is seven by adding one and recursing on the quotient by ten.
definitions.text:
rule digitSevens(X) => 1 +Int digitSevens(X /Int 10)
    requires X >Int 0 andBool X %Int 10 ==Int 7

definitions.rationale: This recurrence defines digitSevens for a positive integer whose last decimal digit is not seven by recursing on the quotient by ten without incrementing.
definitions.text:
rule digitSevens(X) => digitSevens(X /Int 10)
    requires X >Int 0 andBool X %Int 10 =/=Int 7

definitions.rationale: This equation defines fizzContribution as digitSevens when the current integer is divisible by 11.
This equation defines fizzContribution as digitSevens for the remaining eligible case: not divisible by 11 but divisible by 13.
definitions.text:
rule fizzContribution(I) => digitSevens(I)
    requires I %Int 11 =/=Int 0 andBool I %Int 13 ==Int 0

definitions.rationale: This equation completes the fizzContribution definition by assigning zero when the integer is divisible by neither 11 nor 13.
definitions.text:
rule fizzContribution(I) => 0
    requires I %Int 11 =/=Int 0 andBool I %Int 13 =/=Int 0

definitions.rationale: This is the base equation for the interval summary fizzFrom, defining an empty interval's contribution as zero.
definitions.text:
rule fizzFrom(I, N) => 0
    requires I >=Int N

definitions.rationale: This recurrence defines fizzFrom over a nonempty interval as the current fizzContribution plus the summary of the remaining interval.
definitions.text:
rule fizzFrom(I, N) => fizzContribution(I) +Int fizzFrom(I +Int 1, N)
    requires I <Int N

definitions.rationale: This macro equation defines the named INNER-LOOP proof term by expanding it to the exact translated while-loop AST used in the program.
definitions.text:
rule INNER-LOOP =>
    While(Compare(Name("x"), CmpOp(">", Int(0))),
      If(Compare(BinOp("%", Name("x"), Int(10)), CmpOp("==", Int(7))),
        Assign(Name("count"), BinOp("+", Name("count"), Int(1))),
        .Stmts)
      Assign(Name("x"), BinOp("//", Name("x"), Int(10))))

definitions.rationale: This macro equation defines the named OUTER-LOOP proof term by expanding it to the exact translated outer while-loop AST, including the INNER-LOOP macro.
definitions.text:
rule OUTER-LOOP =>
    While(Compare(Name("i"), CmpOp("<", Name("n"))),
      If(BoolOp("or",
          Compare(BinOp("%", Name("i"), Int(11)), CmpOp("==", Int(0))),
          Compare(BinOp("%", Name("i"), Int(13)), CmpOp("==", Int(0)))),
        Assign(Name("x"), Name("i"))
        INNER-LOOP,
        .Stmts)
      Assign(Name("i"), BinOp("+", Name("i"), Int(1))))

source_rules.rationale: This simplification rule supplies integer-addition associativity to normalize symbolic invariant sums; it is an additional algebraic fact, not a summary definition, and prove.sh compiles it into the definition before proving any claims.
